items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to find the surface area of a cube whose edges are [MATH: 3\,\textrm{cm}] in length, like the one shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/156cb2efa915b9c3bf71733c135aec8c]

Content:
The surface area of the cube is the area of all the faces combined. In general, for a cube with sides of length [MATH: s,] there are [MATH: 6] sides, each with area [MATH: \mathcal A = s^2.] So, the surface area is given by

Content:
[MATH: S = 6\mathcal A =6 s^2.]

Content:
To find the surface area of the cube above, we substitute [MATH: s=3 \: \textrm{cm}] into the formula. This gives

Content:
[MATH: S = 6(3\, \text{cm})^2 = 54 \,\textrm{cm}^2.]

Content:
Therefore, the surface area of the cube is [MATH: 54\,\textrm{cm}^2.]

items.title: Finding the Side Length of a Cube Given the Surface Area

sections.normalized_html: The surface area of a cube is [MATH: 240] square units. Find the length of the edges of the cube.
sections.readable_text: The surface area of a cube is [MATH: 240] square units. Find the length of the edges of the cube.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The surface area [MATH: S] of a cube is made of [MATH: 6] congruent squares. So, the area [MATH: \mathcal A] of one face is [MATH: \mathcal{A} = \dfrac{S}{6} = \frac{240}{6} = 40\,.]

Since [MATH: \mathcal A = s^2,] where [MATH: s] is the length of an edge, we can find [MATH: s] as follows: [MATH: s = \sqrt{\mathcal{A}} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}]

Therefore, the length of the edges is [MATH: 2\sqrt{10}] units.
